items.title: Don Albert and Herbert Hall Interview, 1978-08-03
items.q: But I know when people talk about Robichaud today, very often they mean the old man, John, the left-handed bomb.

ctx.x: I see. I haven't got nothing mixed up. I don't know if you meant Joe or John. Mm-hmm. Well, John was all right.

Tanglefoot is simple. That's what I'm like. Pigeon Joe is one. Mm-hmm. That's what I'm saying. Yeah. Yeah. Yeah, boy. Look at this nippy. He's a great dad. But I know when people talk about Robichaud today, very often they mean the old man, John, the left-handed bomb. Yeah. Even though Joe had quite a reputation with his family. Yeah.
And they still say John Robichaud. And they talk about Robichaud.

items.title: Don Albert Interview, 1972-09-18
items.q: There was a left-hand violin player there. I can't recall his name. John Robichaud. No, no.

ctx.x: You said you were in the studio, you told him. Right.

You were there, of course. Well, it's a banjo, uh, like, and, of course, you had another great one, but I don't think he was quite as great as Caffer. It was John, John Morello. Well, he was, he was tremendous. Then, all right, then you go down into, uh, to the clarinets like Lorenzo T.O. Jr. Uh, and the old man, uh, we called him Papai. Uh, huh. That taught all of us how he's a symphony man. Uh, huh. Those guys read music just like the newspaper. I imagine that. I was talking to my professors' daughters last…
